chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Wuheyb ibn Hafs, who said:

We were with Abu Baseer, and Amr ibn Ilyas came to him and said to him, 'O Abu Muhammad! My brother in Halab sent me wealth from the zakat to distribute it in Al-Kufa, but the road was cut off for it. Is there a narration with you regarding it?' He said, 'Yes. I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about this matter, and I did not think anyone would ask me about it ever. So I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom! A man sends his zakat from one land to another, and the road is cut off for it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It has sufficed him, and if it were me, I would pay it again.'

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far (Imam al-Baqir, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on zakat money that is lost in transit before distribution?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the distinction between the legal validity (ajza') of zakat distribution and the recommended caution (i'tidad) in fulfilling the obligation. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms that loss of funds during transit does not invalidate the initial disbursement, yet his personal inclination to re-pay underscores the Shia emphasis on ensuring the poor actually receive their due share.
